Executive summary

This report consolidates 1 RUL experiment run(s) into one dissertation-style artefact. It combines aggregate metrics, model-level diagnostics, train/validation dynamics, held-out bearing predictions, residual analysis, execution logs, and full merged configuration for reproducibility.

  • Rank models by test behavior, not validation alone: validation RMSE selects checkpoints, but held-out bearing plots show whether that checkpoint generalizes.
  • Use multiple metrics: RMSE emphasizes large mistakes, MAE shows typical absolute error, R² shows explained variance, and PHM score captures the asymmetric cost profile used in bearing prognostics.
  • Check runtime and parameters: a lower RMSE is only compelling if its training time and model size are acceptable for the intended research comparison.

Dataset overview

The dataset figure verifies which bearings are used for training, validation, and testing. This is the first place to check if a surprising result is caused by a small held-out split or a different condition mix.

Figure 1.1. Bearings used for training, validation, and testing (length per run).

Health Indicator (HI) features

HI figures show the feature representation actually given to the model. Smooth degradation-aligned traces are easier for sequence models to learn; sparse, noisy, or flat traces usually lead to unstable validation metrics.

Figure 1.2a. Most informative HI feature trace (single feature, after smoothing) for one training bearing.
Figure 1.2b. Full HI matrix (features × time) for the same bearing.

Training dynamics (one metric per figure)

Training dynamics indicate whether the model learned steadily or selected a fragile checkpoint. Watch for a widening train/validation gap, validation RMSE spikes, or early stopping at a very early epoch.

Per-bearing test predictions

Held-out prediction trajectories are the clearest qualitative evidence. A good RUL model should follow the broad monotonic decline and avoid optimistic over-prediction near failure.

Per-bearing residuals over time

Residual plots separate random noise from systematic bias. Positive residuals indicate optimistic RUL estimates; negative residuals indicate conservative estimates.

Configuration

This merged YAML is the exact configuration used for the run: data setup, feature pipeline, model parameters, optimizer schedule, seed, and output paths.

data:
  dataset: phm2012
  root: ../data-bearing/ieee-phm-2012
  cache_dir: ../data-bearing/processed/phm2012
  window_length: 64
  stride_train: 1
  stride_eval: 32
  label_scheme: linear
  smoothing_alpha: 0.1
  n_bands: 5
  batch_size: 128
  num_workers: 8
  train_bearings:
  - '1_1'
  - '1_2'
  - '1_4'
  - '2_1'
  - '2_3'
  - '2_5'
  - '3_1'
  val_bearings:
  - '1_5'
  - '2_2'
  test_bearings:
  - '1_3'
  - '1_6'
  - '1_7'
  - '2_4'
  - '2_6'
  - '2_7'
  - '3_2'
  - '3_3'
model:
  name: mamba_xlstm_net
  d_model: 128
  xlstm_blocks: 3
  slstm_positions:
  - 1
  xlstm_heads: 4
  xlstm_force_fallback: false
  mamba_blocks: 2
  mamba_d_state: 128
  mamba_d_conv: 4
  mamba_expand: 2
  mamba_headdim: 64
  mamba_n_groups: 1
  mamba_rope_fraction: 0.5
  mamba_is_mimo: false
  mamba_mimo_rank: 4
  mamba_chunk_size: 64
  mamba_is_outproj_norm: false
  mamba_bidirectional: true
  mamba_backend: auto
  fusion: gated
  head_hidden: 64
  dropout: 0.1
train:
  max_epochs: 200
  lr: 0.0008
  weight_decay: 0.0003
  xlstm_lr_mult: 0.75
  freeze_xlstm_epochs: 5
  scheduler: cosine
  warmup_epochs: 5
  monotonicity_weight: 0.05
  gradient_clip_val: 1.0
  early_stopping_patience: 9999
  precision: bf16-mixed
  seed: 42
  results_root: results
  run_id: null
